title: Reasoning across millions of documents
summary: How Fact Intelligence prepares the entire case record in advance, helping lawyers find and connect facts across millions of documents.
body_markdown:
A large commercial dispute runs to hundreds of thousands of documents and tens of millions of pages. At that scale, AI can fail quietly: the answer cites real sources and is still wrong, because the model never saw the document that contradicts it.


Fact Intelligence takes a different approach. It reads every page in advance and turns the record into connected, source-linked facts, so the Legora Agent works from the whole case rather than a sample. Fact Intelligence makes that possible across millions of documents.


### Why scale breaks legal AI


Three problems decide whether an AI tool is useful on a large matter. None is solved by a new model alone. They are properties of the work.


#### A model only reasons over what it can see


A million-token context window holds roughly 1,500 pages of evidence, depending on the documents. Against a disclosure set of tens of millions of pages, that is a fraction of a percent. Every model call therefore embeds a selection decision: what the model sees, and what it doesn't. If retrieval misses, the model can reason confidently from an incomplete record.


#### Reading the record costs more than querying it


Scanned PDFs, photographed documents, and faxes need optical character recognition (OCR) to become searchable text. Documents then need parsing, classification, extraction, and indexing. That preparation is where much of the compute goes.


#### The same event appears many times


An email instructs finance to release a payment on March 14. A ledger records a transfer on March 15. A witness statement says the supplier was paid "the following week." These may describe the instruction and settlement of one payment, or separate payments. Working out which is the difference between a chronology and a list of fragments.


### How Fact Intelligence works at scale


#### Read the record before the Agent does


When a file arrives, Fact Intelligence works out what it is before extracting the facts. A transcript is read with awareness of who is speaking. An email is reconstructed in sending order and kept with its attachments as a family. A message thread is reassembled across days. A spreadsheet is read cell by cell. Speaker attribution and cell relationships are part of the evidence.


Routing every page through a frontier model is the fastest way to exhaust a matter budget before ingestion finishes. Where older techniques do the job better and cheaper, we use them: splitting documents by meaning, finding the most information-dense passages, and spotting where defined terms cluster. Models are reserved for the steps that need them. The main one is fact extraction itself, which runs on every page through a gated pipeline where each step verifies the last. The work runs in parallel across compute that scales up for a large production and shuts down when it is done.


#### Process each document once, cite every copy


The same attachment may be forwarded by five people. Identical content is processed once, but each copy still matters, because who sent it and where it sat is evidence in its own right. So a fact extracted once is cited to every document it appears in, and the folder structure the team uploaded stays exactly as it was.


#### Reconcile facts without comparing everything to everything


Comparing every fact against every other fact doesn't scale: with 100,000 facts, that means billions of comparisons. Each fact is reduced to a short signature designed so that similar facts produce similar signatures. Only facts whose signatures are close are compared.


Reducing comparisons is only part of the problem. The comparison work also has to fit in memory. We divide it into bounded groups that workers process independently, rather than loading the whole record at once. Larger groups use approximate nearest-neighbor search to identify candidate matches.


In the payment example, similarity alone does not establish that references describe the same event: an instruction to pay is not evidence that the payment settled, and two payments can have identical descriptions but different dates.


Each assertion keeps its link to the source sentence, because a lawyer will build a pleading on it. References to the same event are connected; separate events remain distinct. Where accounts disagree, the inconsistency is flagged with the sources side by side.


#### Give the Agent a smaller space it can read exhaustively


A structured record of millions of facts is still too large to read in one pass. The Agent uses fast, inexpensive searches over those facts to narrow the matter to a set small enough to examine completely. It then works through that set like a file system. This trades some speed for accuracy, and on a dispute that is the right trade.


### What this means for a case team


You can ask what happened and when, and get a chronology where every entry is sourced and disputed dates are flagged. You can investigate who knew what, and when, or test a witness statement or draft pleading against the record. And when a new document lands late, you can see what it changes, so changing course is still an option.


On customer matters, teams have cut manual factual review by 75% and built a full chronology in an hour rather than days. That time goes back into the work only lawyers can do: judging what the facts mean and deciding what to argue.


A fact that is extracted, connected, and traced to its source sentence can be checked, challenged, and built on. Fact Intelligence is already being used on some of the world's most significant disputes. We're now scaling the technology to bring that same depth of factual analysis to matters involving up to 10 million documents soon.


That is what Fact Intelligence makes possible across millions of documents.
